name: Anat
title: Father of Shamgar
summary: In the Bible, Anat is known only as the father of Shamgar, one of Israel's judges. He is mentioned in the Book of Judges as the father of the hero who struck down 600 Philistines with an oxgoad. The name "Anat" is identical to the name of the Canaanite goddess of war and fertility, Anat, and the expression "son of Anat" may be interpreted as a patronym, a clan designation, or an honorific title for a warrior-like figure. This connection may suggest a mixed cultural background or influence from Canaanite culture in Shamgar's homeland.

keyEvents.title: Shamgar, son of Anat, is mentioned as a judge
keyEvents.description: Shamgar, son of Anat, struck down 600 Philistines with an oxgoad and saved Israel. Anat is identified here as the father of this hero.

keyEvents.title: Shamgar mentioned in the Song of Deborah
keyEvents.description: In the triumphant song of Deborah and Barak, "in the days of Shamgar, son of Anat" is mentioned as a time when roads lay deserted and travelers had to take detours, describing the difficult situation in Israel before Deborah's time.

footnotes.text: The name "Anat" is identical to the name of the Canaanite goddess of war and fertility, Anat, known from Ugaritic texts found in Ras Shamra (ancient Ugarit) in Syria. It is debated whether "son of Anat" (ben Anat) is a patronym (father's name), a clan designation, or an honorific title meaning "warrior," based on the warrior-like character of the goddess Anat.

In Ugaritic texts from around 1400–1200 BC, the goddess Anat is portrayed as a fierce warrior. Some scholars suggest that the title "son of Anat" may have been an honorific for a particularly skilled warrior, rather than a reference to an actual father.

The place name Beth-Anath (Judg 1:33; Josh 19:38) and the personal name Anat appear in an area with strong Canaanite cultural influence. This may indicate that Shamgar's family had connections to a culturally and religiously mixed environment in the border regions between Israelite and Canaanite settlement.

In rabbinic tradition, there is little discussion about Anat as a person, but Shamgar is counted among the minor judges. Some rabbinic sources debate whether Shamgar was actually an Israelite, precisely because of the Canaanite-sounding name "ben Anat".
